Give the same four for meiosis

Use the word clone for a mitosis product and haploid for a meiosis product

sheet.howExamined: B2, 1 hour 15 minutes: 70 marks at Foundation, 80 at Higher, calculator allowed. Usually a late question worth about 6 to 11 marks. Summer 2025 B2 Higher Q9 showed a cell before division and nine chromosome combinations and asked which nuclei meiosis could produce [3], then the process that produces variation [1], then two functions of mitosis [2]. Summer 2023 B2 Foundation Q5 set six statements to sort between mitosis, meiosis and both [6]; Summer 2023 B2 Higher Q9 asked for the products of each division as drawings.
traps: Picking four nuclei because meiosis makes four, instead of checking each one for exactly one chromosome of every pair: in Summer 2025 B2 Higher Q9 many picked four, but only the strongest picked the correct four
Not naming independent assortment as the process that gives variation: very few candidates did in Summer 2025 B2 Higher Q9
Leaving out the word variation when asked what independent assortment does: in Summer 2023 B2 Higher Q9 examiners wanted that word and rarely got it

Drawing the cells made by mitosis or meiosis with the wrong number of cells or chromosomes: the Summer 2023 B2 Higher report says the Q9 drawings showed that many candidates did not understand either process
Giving haploid cells, sperm cells or reduction division to mitosis as well as to meiosis: those were the hardest rows of the Summer 2023 B2 Foundation Q5 table
Not knowing how many chromosomes an egg cell holds: Summer 2023 B2 Foundation Q3 records a surprising gap here. A human gamete holds 23, half of 46

steps.working: Write the test down before looking at any nucleus: one of each pair, so exactly one long and exactly one short.
steps.decision: Meiosis halves the number by taking one chromosome out of every pair. Writing the test first stops you counting to four and stopping.

steps.working: Work along the row: (i) one long, one short — yes; (ii) fails the test — no; (iii) one long, one short — yes.
steps.decision: One nucleus at a time, and answer both questions about each before moving on.

steps.working: Finish the second row, and the answer is (i), (iii), (vi).
steps.decision: Check the count at the end: meiosis makes four cells, and here 3 of the six drawn pass the test, which is fine — the diagram shows a selection, not the whole set.

options: Because a nucleus missing a whole pair could not have come from meiosis
Because meiosis always produces exactly the nuclei drawn
Because the shaded chromosomes must all end up together
whyMenu.explain: Meiosis separates the members of each pair, so every product holds one of each. A nucleus with both of one pair, or with neither, cannot be a product.

steps.working: Name the division before doing any arithmetic: a sperm cell is a gamete, so it is made by meiosis.
steps.decision: The division decides what happens to the number. Meiosis halves, mitosis keeps, fertilisation adds.

steps.working: Halve: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 chromosomes in the sperm cell.
steps.decision: Reduction division: one chromosome out of each pair goes to each gamete.

steps.working: At fertilisation 4 + 4 = 8, and mitosis keeps that, so every embryo cell holds 8.
steps.decision: Two gametes join, so the halves add back to a whole. Mitosis then copies that number over and over.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: 4 in a sperm cell, and 8 in a cell of the embryo.

data.caption: A parent cell with 46 chromosomes divides. Fill in the six empty cells.
rows: number of divisions of the nucleus

steps.working: Fill the mitosis column first: 1 division, 2 cells, 46 chromosomes.
steps.decision: Mitosis is the simpler column: one division, and nothing changes about the chromosomes.
Two divisions is what makes four cells; the two numbers go together, so getting one right checks the other.

steps.working: Last, the chromosome number for meiosis: 46 ÷ 2 = 23.
steps.decision: Reduction division. Check it: 23 + 23 = 46 at fertilisation, which is where the number has to end up.

items.stem: Before we start, three things from the last topic. Where in a cell are the chromosomes found?

options.feedback: In the nucleus, which is where both kinds of division take place.
Only a bacterium keeps its genetic material loose in the cytoplasm.
The membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.
The mitochondria release energy by respiration.

items.stem: How many chromosomes are there in a human body cell?

options.feedback: 23 pairs, so 46 chromosomes.
That is the number of pairs, and also a gamete's number.
That counts each chromosome of a pair twice.
One chromosome carries many genes, not one each.

options.text: a sex cell, such as a sperm cell or an ovum
options.feedback: A sex cell. Making them is the one job of meiosis.
That is a zygote, made when two gametes join.

options.text: a cell that has no nucleus
options.feedback: Gametes have a nucleus; it simply holds half the usual number of chromosomes.

options.text: a cell of the skin or the gut
options.feedback: Those are body cells, and they divide by mitosis.

items.stem: How many times does the nucleus divide in meiosis?

options.feedback: Twice, which is what gives four cells rather than two.
One division is mitosis. Meiosis divides twice.
Four is the number of cells produced, not the number of divisions.

options.text: it does not divide at all
options.feedback: Meiosis is a cell division; the nucleus must divide for cells to be produced.

items.stem: How many daughter cells does one cell produce by mitosis?

options.feedback: Two, and they are clones of the parent cell.
Four is meiosis's number.
One is the number of divisions, not the number of cells produced.
Mitosis always gives two cells from one, in every tissue.

items.stem: A cell with 46 chromosomes divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes are in each daughter cell?
items.skill: Apply the chromosome rule to mitosis

options.feedback: Mitosis duplicates the chromosomes exactly, so the number does not change.
Halving is what meiosis does. Mitosis keeps the number the same.
Nothing doubles the number in a daughter cell; the copies are shared between the two cells.

options.text: it varies from cell to cell
options.feedback: Mitosis is an exact duplication, so every daughter cell holds the same number.

items.stem: A cell with 46 chromosomes divides by meiosis. How many chromosomes are in each cell produced?
items.skill: Apply the chromosome rule to meiosis

options.feedback: Reduction division: one of each pair, so half the number.
That leaves the number unchanged, which is mitosis.
Doubling happens at fertilisation, when two gametes join.

options.text: the same as the parent cell
options.feedback: Meiosis is named a reduction division because the number goes down.

items.stem: Which statement describes the cells produced by meiosis?

options.text: all genetically different from one another
options.feedback: Independent assortment gives each one a different combination.

options.text: all genetically identical to the parent cell
options.feedback: That describes mitosis.

options.text: identical to each other but different from the parent
options.feedback: The four differ from each other as well.
Clone is the word for a mitosis product.

items.stem: Where in the human body does meiosis take place?

options.text: in the ovaries and the testes
options.feedback: Only there, and only to make gametes.

options.text: in every tissue of the body
options.feedback: That is mitosis, which grows, replaces and repairs everywhere.

options.text: in the skin and the lining of the gut
options.feedback: Those tissues are renewed by mitosis.
Bone marrow makes blood cells, by mitosis.

items.stem: Which of these is NOT one of the three uses of mitosis the specification lists?
items.skill: Recall the three jobs of mitosis

options.feedback: Correct: making gametes is the job of meiosis, not mitosis.
Growth is one of the three.
Replacing worn-out cells is one of the three.
Repairing damaged tissue is one of the three.

items.stem: Name the process in meiosis that reassorts the chromosomes and produces variation.

options.feedback: Independent assortment. Examiners report it is very rarely written.
Crossing over is not on this specification, and it is not the term the scheme wants.
Fertilisation happens after meiosis, when two gametes join.
A mutation is a random change in a gene or in the number of chromosomes, not the shuffling of whole chromosomes into gametes.

parts.workedSolution: Mitosis divides the nucleus once, while meiosis divides it twice. Mitosis therefore produces two daughter cells and meiosis produces four. The two cells produced by mitosis are genetically identical to the parent cell, so they are clones of it, whereas the four cells produced by meiosis are all genetically different from one another. Mitosis keeps the chromosome number the same, so a cell with 46 chromosomes gives cells with 46; meiosis halves it, so the same cell gives gametes with 23, and that is why meiosis is called a reduction division. The body uses mitosis for growth, for replacing worn-out cells and for repairing damaged tissue, and it happens all over the body. Meiosis happens only in the ovaries and the testes, where it makes gametes, and independent assortment shuffles the chromosomes so that the gametes differ, which is the source of variation.

findTheMistake.stem:
Seán is asked: 'For each statement, say whether it is true for mitosis only, for meiosis only, or for both. [3]'
His answers:

the cells it produces are haploid: both

findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Lines 1 and 3 are right, and each earns its mark. Line 2 gives haploid cells to both divisions. Haploid means one chromosome from each pair, so the number has been halved, and only meiosis does that. Mitosis copies every chromosome first, so both of its cells keep every pair.
correction: it repairs the skin after a graze: mitosis only
the cells it produces are haploid: meiosis only
it is a kind of cell division: both

findTheMistake.stem:
Aoife is asked: 'A human body cell divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes are in each daughter cell? [1]'
Her working:

findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Line 1 is right. Line 2 is the rule for the wrong division: only meiosis halves the chromosome number, and only because it is making gametes. Mitosis duplicates the chromosomes exactly first, so both daughter cells end up with a full set.
correction: mitosis duplicates them exactly, then shares one full set to each daughter cell
findTheMistake.feedback: No marks, because the one mark here was the number. A quick check: if every division halved the number, a body cell would run out of chromosomes within a few days of growing.

findTheMistake.stem:

findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: The second line describes a real idea, but the first names a process the specification explicitly leaves out. CCEA asks for independent assortment: the chromosomes of each pair are dealt out to the new cells at random, so every gamete gets a different combination.
correction: the chromosomes of each pair are dealt out at random, so every gamete gets a different combination
findTheMistake.feedback: One mark of the two. Learn the two words on their own: independent assortment is named in the specification, and crossing over is named as not required.

insight.ruleToRemember: Mitosis makes two identical diploid cells (growth, replacing worn-out cells, repairing damaged tissue). Meiosis makes four genetically different haploid gametes with half the chromosome number; independent assortment is the source of the variation. Count chromosomes: 46 in body cells and germ cells, 23 in gametes.
insight.aStarSignal: Choosing the products from diagrams by chromosome number and combination, and using 'independent assortment' and 'variation' unprompted.
